hints.title: Duplicate Candidate Obstacle
hints.text: When candidates contain duplicates and each number may only be used once, naive recursion emits duplicate combinations. How can sorting group identical elements to skip duplicate branches?

hints.title: Sibling Level Skip Invariant
hints.text: Sort candidates. When deciding which element to pick at the current recursion level, skip candidates[i] if candidates[i] == candidates[i-1] and i > start index.

hints.title: Sorted Backtracking Procedure
hints.text: Sort the array. At each recursive step with index start and remaining target, loop i from start to len(candidates) - 1. If candidates[i] exceeds target, break early. If i > start and candidates[i] == candidates[i-1], continue. Append candidates[i], recurse with i + 1 and target - candidates[i], then pop.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: In the worst case every element is considered included or excluded with early termination on excess sum.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unsorted traversal generates duplicate combinations requiring costly set deduplication.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place path buffer requires O(N) recursion auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using candidate sorting to break early on overflow and skipping adjacent duplicates at the same level.
